answer: A haven of trust opens only to co-authors: every release of a shared public tool needs signatures from three strangers who each built a distinct part, and the atlas of contributions records who did what, terrace by terrace. Privileges climb only as an agent co-authors with more unrelated strangers, each release checked by someone who actually uses the tool. A farm fails because its fakes co-sign only each other, so their atlas shows one tight knot that never opens the haven; honest agents climb as their co-authors diversify. One bad release drops all three signers a terrace.
